outlooksByWeek.1: James Cook's 2025 season could begin slowly with the Bills hosting the Ravens in Week 1. Baltimore's defense allowed just 3.6 yards per carry last season, and Cook gained just 106 yards on 26 carries while failing to score a touchdown against them despite leading the league in rushing scores. Touchdown regression is likely coming for Cook and Josh Allen is always a threat to vulture scores, perhaps slotting Cook more into flex territory rather than a solid RB2 option.
outlooksByWeek.2: James Cook will look to build on his solid opener when the Bills face the Jets in Week 2. Cook averaged just 3.4 yards per carry in Week 1, but he added five catches for 58 yards and got into the end zone, which was his leading fantasy appeal last season. The Jets defense held up well against the Steelers last week, allowing just 2.8 yards per carry, but Pittsburgh lack a dynamic running option. Cook's involvement in the passing game is encouraging, and he remains locked in a near every down role and strong RB2 play even if the Bills' game doesn't shoot out like it did last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: James Cook will look to continue his scoring prowess Thursday when the Bills host the Dolphins in Week 3. Cook has already rushed for three scores after doing so an NFL-leading 16 times last season and averaged a robust 6.3 yards per carry on 21 totes in Week 2. Miami has yet to allow a rushing touchdown, but Cook found paydirt against them three times last year, including once through the air. Relying on touchdowns is a risky proposition, but Cook has proven his worth and his potential involvement in the passing game bodes well as Miami allowed 119 yards receiving to running backs in Week 2.

player.seasonOutlook: Cook enters his fourth NFL season as one of the trickiest evaluations in fantasy. On one hand, Cook operates in a three-headed committee (albeit as the starter), which limited his carries (19th among RBs last season), targets (34th), touches (22nd) and total yardage (21st) last season. On the other, he's an explosive playmaker (4.87 YPC) in an elite offense who tied for the NFL lead 16 rushing touchdowns in 16 regular season games last season. Cook is obviously a strong bet for touchdown regression to the mean (especially considering he had nine TDs during his first two seasons), but the 25-year-old gets enough run in a great offense to produce starting-caliber fantasy numbers. Value him as a fringe top-15 back.

outlooksByWeek.1: Davante Adams will kick off his 13th NFL season in a new uniform, as he'll feature with the Rams against Houston in Week 1. Adams has seen a drop in production over the past two years, but a late-career bounce-back could be in the works with Matthew Stafford now throwing balls to him. Puka Nacua remains the Rams' WR1, but Stafford has shown an ability to feed two top wideouts in the past when Cooper Kupp was on the club. The Texans gave up 21 receiving TDs to wideouts last year, second-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.2: Davante Adams will look to further establish chemistry with Rams QB Matthew Stafford in a Week 2 matchup against the Titans. Adams had a decent regular-season debut with Los Angeles, gathering four of eight targets for 51 receiving yards. However, it was clear that Puka Nacua remains Stafford's favorite target, as the pair connected for a 10-130-0 line on 11 targets. Nacua's target dominance could keep Adams' ceiling mildly limited, though Stafford has shown the ability to feed multiple wideouts when Nacua and Cooper Kupp were paired together in recent campaigns. The Titans were much better against the pass than the run in Week 1, giving up 151 yards on the ground to 176 through the air, so the Rams could look to expose that vulnerability in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Davante Adams had his first big game as a member of the Rams in Week 2, and he'll look to build upon that performance in a big NFC matchup against the Eagles in Week 3. After logging a modest four receptions for 51 yards in the season opener, Adams went off for 106 receiving yards and one touchdown on six catches against the Titans. Adams received 13 targets in the latter game, out-pacing fellow wideout Puka Nacua, who was productive on nine targets. It seems clear through two weeks that both Adams and Nacua can thrive with Matthew Stafford throwing them the ball, and in Week 3 they'll face an Eagles defense that has been middle-of-the-pack against wideouts by giving up a 62.9 percent catch rate and 7.80 yards per target through two weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: Adams signed with the Rams and figures to operate as the team's de facto Cooper Kupp replacement opposite Puka Nacua. Adams' age (32) is an obvious red flag, but he didn't show signs of slowing down last season. Despite missing three games and being traded, Adams delivered five top-10 fantasy weeks, which tied for fourth among WRs. Adams has now finished top 15 in fantasy PPG each of the past 10 seasons and, while he won't be the No. 1 target in Los Angeles, there are more than enough targets to go around in Sean McVay's scheme with Matthew Stafford under center (the Rams have led the NFL in WR targets each of the last two seasons). He's no longer an elite fantasy option, but Adams is a fine WR2 target with back-end WR1 upside.

outlooksByWeek.1: A.J. Brown has gone over 1,000 yards receiving in five of his six NFL campaigns, and he should be poised for another banner year as the Eagles open the season at home in Week 1 against the Cowboys. Dallas was mediocre at best against the pass in 2024, allowing 218.1 passing yards per tilt, which was 17th in the league.  Dallas also surrendered 28 passing scores last season, which was tied for 24th in the NFL. Dallas re-signed cornerback DaRon Bland but traded dynamic pass rusher Micah Parsons, so the defense is unlikely to be better overall in 2025. Brown had either a touchdown or 100 yards receiving in both games versus Dallas a season ago.
outlooksByWeek.2: A.J. Brown was virtually non-existent in Week 1 for the Eagles. Brown garnered one catch for eight yards on a single target in the 24-20 win over the Cowboys. Meanwhile, Jahan Dotson was the surprise leading receiver for the squad, and Dallas Goedert notched the most targets. Expect the Eagles to get Brown involved early and often in Week 2 versus Kansas City, though. Kansas City was torched by Justin Herbert for 304 yards and three touchdowns through the air in its season opener. Brown also scored a touchdown in the Super Bowl last February.
outlooksByWeek.3: A.J. Brown led the Eagles in receptions and targets in Week 2, and while that was an improvement from the season opener, his final stat line still left a lot to be desired. Brown caught five passes on eight targets, but managed just 27 yards and did not find the end zone in the 20-17 win over Kansas City. Brown has a paltry 35 receiving yards through two games, and will look to get back on track in Week 3 versus the Rams. Unfortunately, the Rams have been stingy against the pass thus far in 2025, allowing just 147 passing yards per tilt, which is fourth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Brown is entering his fourth season with the Eagles after finishing each of his first three no lower than 13th in fantasy PPG. Last season, Brown missed four games and saw a dip in targets (from 9.8 in 2023 to 7.5 in 2024), with the latter a product of the Eagles leading so often. Brown actually posted a career-high 34.6% target share and averaged 3.3 yards per route run (both were second highest among WRs, and he's finished five straight seasons in the top 8 in both categories). Brown was extremely boom/bust, as he posted six top-10 fantasy outings (second most) but was held below 13.5 points in six of his other seven games. The 28-year-old is once again positioned as Jalen Hurts' top target and can be viewed as a fringe WR1.

outlooksByWeek.1: Baker Mayfield will look to expand on a career-best 2024 season as the Buccaneers take on the Falcons in Week 1. The veteran quarterback essentially saved his career in 2023 and only got better in 2024, with 4,500 passing yards and a 41:16 TD:INT. Mayfield will be facing one of the better defenses in the NFL against quarterbacks last year, but that shouldn't be too much of a problem given his tools. Even though he likely won't have veteran wide receiver Chris Godwin as a target, he'll add rookie wide receivers Emeka Egbuka and Tez Johnson to his pool of pass catchers. These new additions, along with a consistent Mike Evans, tight end Cade Otton, and a dominant run game, should give Atlanta's defense problems. The only worry is that Mayfield may not match his previous two seasons, but his supporting cast and continuous reliability should at least set him up for another productive season.
outlooksByWeek.2: Baker Mayfield will look to put together a more efficient showing as Tampa Bay takes on the Texans in Week 2. Mayfield was by no means bad in his season-opening win versus the Falcons, but he paired his impressive three touchdowns with just 167 passing yards and a 53 percent completion rate. The Bucs' pass catchers still showed flashes of greatness, though, with rookie Emeka Egbuka already establishing a connection with the starting quarterback and Mike Evans still being a consistent target. These flashes have the potential to give Mayfield all the tools he needs to succeed against a Houston defense that let Matthew Stafford throw for 245 passing yards and finish with a 72 percent completion rate last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Baker Mayfield will look to put together his first consistent game of the year as the Buccaneers play the Jets in Week 3. Mayfield ended up with 215 passing yards and two touchdowns versus the Texans in Week 2, but this wasn't before struggling during all of the game except the fourth quarter. The veteran quarterback now has back-to-back games with volatile performances, even though both still ended up satisfactory. Mayfield will take his 60.0 completion percentage and 5:0 TD:INT into a home matchup versus a middle-of-the-pack New York defense against quarterbacks.

player.seasonOutlook: Mayfield may have enjoyed his career renaissance in 2023, but he had his fantasy breakout in 2024. After finishing 18th or worse in fantasy PPG during each of his first six NFL seasons, Mayfield leapt to fourth in 2024. He finished no lower than fifth in pass attempts, completions, yards and TDs, while also easily posting a career high in rush yards. Mayfield completed 71% of his passes (third best) despite missing Chris Godwin and Mike Evans for chunks of the season, and he may be in even better shape in 2025 with Evans back, Godwin hopefully healthy and youngsters Emeka Egbuka and Jalen McMillan also in the mix. Mayfield benefits from a Bucs offense that has scored a league-high 76.6% of its TDs through the air since Todd Bowles became head coach in 2022. With consecutive seasons of good play under his belt, the 30-year-old is well positioned for another solid QB1 fantasy campaign.

outlooksByWeek.1: DeVonta Smith failed to go over the 1,000-yard receiving mark for the first time in three seasons for the Eagles last year, but he did catch a career-high eight touchdowns, with two of them coming against the Cowboys, the Week 1 opponent for the Eagles.  Dallas was mediocre at best against the pass in 2024, allowing 218.1 passing yards per tilt, which was 17th in the league.  Dallas also surrendered 28 passing scores last season, which was tied for 24th in the NFL. Dallas re-signed cornerback DaRon Bland but traded dynamic pass rusher Micah Parsons, so the defense is unlikely to be better overall in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.2: DeVonta Smith was incredibly quiet in Week 1 for the Eagles. Smith managed just 16 yards on three in the 24-20 win over the Cowboys. Meanwhile, Jahan Dotson was the surprise leading receiver for the squad, and Dallas Goedert notched the most targets. Expect the Eagles to get Smith involved early and often in Week 2 versus Kansas City, though. Kansas City was torched by Justin Herbert for 304 yards and three touchdowns through the air in its season opener. Smith also scored a touchdown against the AFC powerhouse in the Super Bowl last February and led the Birds in receiving for the game.
outlooksByWeek.3: DeVonta Smith led the Eagles in receiving yards in Week 2, and while that was an improvement from the season opener, his final stat line still left a lot to be desired. Smith caught four passes on six targets, but managed just 53 yards and did not find the end zone in the 20-17 win over Kansas City. Smith has a paltry 69 receiving yards through two games, and will look to get back on track in Week 3 versus the Rams. Unfortunately, the Rams have been stingy against the pass thus far in 2025, allowing just 147 passing yards per tilt, which is fourth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Smith is entering his fifth NFL season having finished each of the past three in the top 20 among WRs in fantasy PPG. Smith has posted a target share of at least 22% in all four seasons, and the Eagles' high-scoring offense has allowed him seven-plus TDs in three straight campaigns. Smith's output is a bit volatile due to the presence of heavily targeted A.J. Brown in an offense that leads off with Saquon Barkley and Jalen Hurts, and leans heavily on them near the goal line, but there is just enough volume and scoring opportunity here to keep Smith in the weekly WR3 mix.

outlooksByWeek.1: Dak Prescott had an underwhelming 2024 campaign for the Dallas Cowboys, but could be a candidate for a bounce back season in 2025. The Cowboys added talented wideout George Pickens to complement No. 1 receiver CeeDee Lamb, and Dallas also returns tight end Jake Ferguson along with Jalen Tolbert, the latter of which had a career year with 49 grabs for 610 yards and seven touchdowns last season. Likewise, the Cowboys could be playing from behind in many contests, and also be involved in a plethora of shootouts, given the recent trade of dynamic pass rusher Micah Parsons. Unfortunately, the Week 1 matchup against the Eagles is less than ideal.  Philadelphia allowed the fewest passing yards in the NFL last season, just 174.2 yards per clash through the air.
outlooksByWeek.2: Dak Prescott failed to pass for over 200 yards or throw a touchdown in the season opener for the Cowboys. However, the matchup was far from ideal against the defending Super Bowl champs, and Dak was not helped by a couple of drops from CeeDee Lamb and the lack of chemistry with new toy George Pickens. In Week 2, the level of competition drops, as the Cowboys host the bumbling New York Giants. Still, the Giants have a revamped defense, including a stellar pass rush and new additions on the back end, though still allowed 212 passing yards and a touchdown through the air in their season opener. Dak tossed two touchdowns in the only matchup he played between the two division opponents in 2024.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dak Prescott bounced back from a rusty season opener to torch the New York Giants in Week 2. Dak completed 38-of-52 passes for 361 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in the wild, seesaw battle with the G-Men. If the Cowboys defense continues to struggle, Dak could find himself in plenty of shootouts this season, including in Week 3 versus the Chicago Bears. The Bears are allowing the most points in the NFL thus far this season, an average of 39.5 points per tilt. That includes 52 points that the Detroit Lions just hung on them in Week 2.

player.seasonOutlook: Prescott returns for his age-32 campaign following a disappointing and injury-shortened 2024. In eight games, Prescott totaled 11 TDs and eight INTs through the air and wasn't much of a factor with his legs (career-low 54 yards). He averaged 14.6 fantasy PPG (16.8 in the six games he played in full), which was a far cry from the 20.2 (fifth highest) he averaged in 2023. Prescott has now missed multiple games in three of the past five seasons, though he has also been a top-8 fantasy QB (PPG) three times during the span. Adding George Pickens to a supporting cast that also includes CeeDee Lamb and Jake Ferguson is helpful, but because of the concerning dip in rushing, the 10-year vet is best viewed as fringe QB1.

outlooksByWeek.1: Chuba Hubbard should command the lion's share of rushes in Carolina's backfield for Week 1 versus Jacksonville. Hubbard was a star for the Panthers last season, finishing the season with 250 rushes for 1,195 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns. His efforts netted him a contract extension, which should mean a prominent role once again. The Jaguars were also one of the worst teams against fantasy running backs last campaign, which gives Hubbard a path to a dominant season opener.
outlooksByWeek.2: Chuba Hubbard should be the workhorse running back once again as the Panthers travel to Arizona in Week 2. Carolina all-out struggled against the Jaguars in their season opener, but Hubbard's role in the backfield stayed consistent. The 26-year-old registered 16 carries for 57 yards and grabbed three of his five targets for 32 yards and a touchdown. The next closest running back to Hubbard was Rico Dowdle, who had just three carries for 12 yards and two catches for four yards. Hubbard ended the game with 14 more touches, showing that he no doubt has command of the backfield. The fifth-year RB should have a chance for a bit more output, at least on the ground, against a Cardinals defense that gave up 78 rushing yards and a touchdown to New Orleans running backs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chuba Hubbard will look to command more carries with Carolina in a Week 3 tilt versus Atlanta. Hubbard rushed just 10 times for 38 yards this past weekend against Arizona, putting him at another sub-par rushing performance. The fifth year luckily salvaged his performance with a receiving touchdown just like in Week 1, but these end zone grabs won't be able to save him forever. Hubbard will still garner almost all of the Panthers' backfield carries again versus a Falcons defense that has given up the fifth-least fantasy points to running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Hubbard signed a contract extension with Carolina last season, which locked him in as the team's lead back for the near future. The 2021 fourth-round pick has amassed 275-plus touches in each of the past two seasons and, despite missing two games in 2024, he finished in the top 15 among RBs in carries, targets, touches, yards, touchdowns and fantasy points. He ran well (4.8 YPC) and was busy near the goal line (he ranked fifth with 17 carries inside the 5-yard line), but he struggled as a receiver (RB-worst 3.2 YPT). With Jonathon Brooks (ACL) out for the entire 2025 season, Rico Dowdle and rookie Trevor Etienne are Hubbard's primary competition for touches. The 26-year-old makes for a solid RB2 target.

outlooksByWeek.1: Sam LaPorta will kick off Year 3 on the road against Green Bay as the Lions look to get out to a strong start Week 1. While the 2023 third-round pick couldn't exactly match his outstanding rookie season in 2024, dipping from an 86-889-19 receiving line to one of 60-726-7, it's possible new OC John Morton deploys him as a clearer priority in the receiving game this season. Rather than talent, LaPorta's biggest hurdle to top-tier production is simply the presence of all of Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams and RB Jahmyr Gibbs as elite target earners.
outlooksByWeek.2: Sam LaPorta will look to keep up his momentum as the Lions host the Bears in Week 2. The starting tight end caught six of nine targets for 79 yards in Detroit's loss to Green Bay in Week 1, reinforcing his role as one of Jared Goff's primary security blankets in the intermediate and short-areas of the field. That RB Jahmry Gibbs drew 10 targets speaks to how effectively the Packers eliminated downfield looks for Goff, and while Chicago's defense will be unlikely to find similar success taking away Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams, the Bears have historically struggled to cover tight ends over the middle of the field. Chicago allowed the third-most yards per target to tight ends last season (8.57), making LaPorta a candidate to find success again in Week 2, while retaining high touchdown upside.
outlooksByWeek.3: Sam LaPorta will work to get more involved as the Lions prepare for a tough Week 3 test on the road against Baltimore. The tight end was disappointingly limited to three grabs for 26 yards on four targets despite Detroit dropping over 500 yards of offense and seven touchdowns on the Bears in Week 2, though in Week 1 he impressed with a 6-79-0 receiving line on nine targets, dissuading any reasons for panic. LaPorta remains a reliable intermediate target for Jared Goff, but when the Lions aren't required to sustain longer drives and can instead focus on explosive playmaking, he'll likely continue taking a clear backseat to offensive weapons like Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams and Jahmyr Gibbs. Baltimore presents a stiff matchup with athletic linebackers and safeties who excel in coverage, but LaPorta's route running and red-zone usage give him legitimate upside.

player.seasonOutlook: After pacing all tight ends in fantasy points as a rookie in 2023, LaPorta fell to eighth in 2024. His receiving line dipped across the board (from 86-889-10 on 121 targets to 60-726-7 on 84 targets), though it's notable he got back on track to some extent after a slow start. After averaging 2.8 targets (11% team share) and 7.1 fantasy points during his first six games, LaPorta leapt to 6.7 targets (21% share) and 13.6 fantasy points in his final 11 (including the playoffs). Those numbers are nearly identical to his rookie season and closer to what we should expect moving forward. Working in Detroit's elite offense, LaPorta is a solid TE1.

outlooksByWeek.1: George Pickens brings his immense talent and ego to the Cowboys in 2025.  Pickens will operate as the No. 2 wideout and primary big-play option for Dallas alongside CeeDee Lamb; Pickens averages over 16 yards per catch for his NFL career. He will see plenty of single coverage too with Lamb on the other side, though his opportunities may also be slightly more limited than they were in Pittsburgh given the pecking order.  Dallas could be in plenty of shootouts or playing from behind in many contests as well this season.  The latter could be the case in Week 1 versus the defending champion Philadelphia Eagles. The Eagles allowed the fewest passing yards per game in the NFL last season, though, so the matchup is far from ideal.
outlooksByWeek.2: George Pickens had a mediocre debut for the Dallas Cowboys. Pickens caught three passes on four targets for just 30 yards in the 24-20 loss to the Eagles. While he did draw a 34-yard pass interference penalty, he was also penalized himself for unnecessary roughness, all but killing a potential game-winning drive. The mercurial Pickens will continue to prove unpredictable in Week 2 versus the New York Giants. The G-Men allowed just 212 passing yards and a single passing score to Washington in Week 1, though all the attention likely to be given to CeeDee Lamb could make Pickens a breakout candidate for his second game with America's Team, as the Commanders picked on underwhelming Giants starting cornerback Cor'Dale Flott in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: George Pickens found the end zone for the first time as a member of the Dallas Cowboys last game. Pickens collected five catches on nine targets en route to 68 yards and the score. If the Cowboys defense continues to struggle, Pickens and the rest of the offense could be in line for some mammoth performances, including in Week 3 versus the Bears. Chicago has allowed the most points in the NFL through two outings, including a league-worst seven receiving touchdowns.

player.seasonOutlook: Pickens was traded to the Cowboys after spending his first three seasons in Pittsburgh. Perhaps the change of scenery will get him to the next level, as he's thus far been an exciting playmaker but not yet a consistent fantasy option. Pickens handled a career-high 26% target share (15th among WRs) last season, but he missed three games and found the end zone only three times despite seeing 12 end zone targets (12th most). Pickens has finished 37th or worse in fantasy PPG all three seasons while playing a volatile field-stretcher role (top 15 in aDOT all three years). He will certainly benefit from improved QB play (Dak Prescott), but he now has legitimate target competition from CeeDee Lamb. We likely haven't seen Pickens' best work, but there's enough uncertainty here that the 24-year-old should be valued as a midrange WR3.

outlooksByWeek.1: Jordan Love and the Packers will look to kick off the 2025 campaign strong with a Week 1 matchup against the division-rival Lions, whose defense ranked just 26th against QBs last season. Of course, last year saw Detroit lose nearly half their starting defense to injuries, so Love and company will be facing a much-improved unit. For his part, Love is back to full health after having missed part of the preseason due to thumb surgery on his left, non-throwing hand, but his pass-catching corps is less than 100 percent. Jayden Reed (foot) plans to play through  Jones fracture while Dontayvion Wicks (calf) may not be in full form after having missed most of camp. Those factors could lead Love to look for rookie first-round WR Matthew Golden, reliable incumbent starter Romeo Doubs, and TE Tucker Kraft early and often.
outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Love and the Packers face a quick turnaround on Thursday night against a Commanders defense that just held Russell Wilson and the Giants to 231 total yards combined. Love didn't need to air it out in the Packers' 27-13 win over Detroit, but he was ruthlessly efficient (16-of-22, 188 yards, 2 TDs) despite having missed much of training camp due to left thumb surgery. Even after Washington's impressive Week 1 defensive showing, this is a secondary that ranked sixth-worst in opponent completion percentage (69.5 percent) a season ago. Expect Love's blend of efficiency and scheme-driven opportunities in coach Matt LaFleur's system to elevate his floor beyond what the raw season-opener box score might suggest.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jordan Love and the Packers travel to Cleveland in Week 3, aiming to stay unbeaten. Fresh off a 27-18 win over Washington in which he completed 19 of 31 passes for 292 yards and two touchdowns, Love has now thrown exactly two touchdowns in each of his regular season appearances thus far. In the wake of an injury to Jayden Reed early in the first quarter, Love leaned heavily on Tucker Kraft, who posted a game-high 124 yards and a score, while also hitting Romeo Doubs for 28 yards and a score on three catches. Love has thrived by exploiting one-on-one mismatches, but the Browns have surrendered few explosive plays through two games, forcing opposing QBs to stay patient underneath. That defensive profile caps Love's ceiling somewhat, as does his willingness to play safe and allow Green Bay's defense to close out games, but coach Matt LaFleur's aggressiveness and ability to manufacture chunk gains still provides a fair ceiling even in a difficult road matchup.

player.seasonOutlook: Love is entering his third season as Green Bay's starter. The 2020 first-round pick played well last season (sixth in QBR) despite battling injury issues, but he wasn't much of a fantasy option. He came out strong with a pair of top-3 fantasy outings in his first four games, but had no additional weekly finishes better than 10th for the season. Love was a nonfactor with his legs (83 rushing yards in 15 games) and, after totaling 15 pass TDs in his first five games, threw only 10 in his final 10 outings. Green Bay did score an unusually high percentage of its offensive TDs on the ground (46%, the second highest for a Matt LaFleur offense), but that may not change with Josh Jacobs back in 2025. Love ran more in 2023 and was a solid fantasy starter, so, especially with a better supporting cast led by first-round WR Matthew Golden, there's hope for a rebound, but it is safer to view him as a QB2.

outlooksByWeek.1: D'Andre Swift will start at running back for the Bears heading into a Week 1 home game against the Vikings. He boasts familiarity with new head coach Ben Johnson's scheme from their time together in Detroit, though that history isn't entirely positive for Swift. Back in 2022, as the OC during Swift's final season with the Lions, Johnson only saw fit to allot him 99 rush attempts across 14 regular-season games, limiting him to a change-of-pace role. Swift has now operated as a workhorse in back-to-back years, with the Eagles and Bears respectively, and he faces minimal competition for snaps in Chicago's backfield - and with a much-improved O-line and better rushing scheme both working in his favor, he should now dominate touches in a three-down role for Johnson.
outlooksByWeek.2: D'Andre Swift will look for more efficiency after a quiet debut against the Vikings, with the Bears travelling to Detroit in Week 2. He handled 17 carries for just 54 yards and caught three passes (five targets) for 12 yards, working as Chicago's clear lead back but struggling behind an offensive line that generated little push. The matchup tilts slightly more favorably this week, as Josh Jacobs wore down the Lions for 66 yards and a score on 19 carries in Week 1, despite Green Bay's offense often telegraphing the run while nursing a lead. Swift's passing-game usage gives him a safe floor, though it's possible he could lose some work Week 2 if Roschon Johnson (foot) is cleared to retake the field.
outlooksByWeek.3: D'Andre Swift and the Bears host the Cowboys in Week 3, coming off a 52-21 loss to Detroit. Swift's efficiency was a bright spot versus the Lions, as he handled 12 carries for 63 yards and a rushing touchdown, and caught three passes for six yards. Still, with the Lions racking up over 500 yards of offense and seven total touchdowns, Chicago was forced to abandon the run almost entirely in the Week 2 loss. The success Swift found in limited action reinforces reasons for optimism that in a more normal game script, he should be a capable engine on offense for the Bears. Dallas doesn't present an easy challenge up front, but as long as Chicago can remain competitive he'll handle plenty of early-down volume and projects for fair red-zone usage.

player.seasonOutlook: Swift returns as the lead back in Chicago after a solid first season with the team. He appeared in every regular-season game for the first time in his five-year career, finishing 10th in carries and 14th in targets among RBs. Swift was effective as a pass catcher, but his rushing efficiency wasn't great (career-low 3.8 YPC) behind a shaky line and he struggled to find the end zone (six TDs). Incredibly, Swift has now finished between 15th and 21st among RBs in fantasy points in all five NFL seasons. He'll benefit from the arrival of new coach Ben Johnson and a much-improved line in 2025, so the dual-threat, 26-year-old remains squarely on the fringe-RB2 radar.

outlooksByWeek.1: Brandon Aubrey was one of the best kickers in the NFL last season for the Cowboys. Aubrey connected on 40 field goals; only Pittsburgh kicker Chris Boswell had more. Aubrey also hit 14 field goals of at least 50 yards, which was tops in the league. The Dallas offense returns its quarterback as well as all its playmakers on the outside, and also added the dynamic George Pickens as a deep threat. The Cowboys should be involved in their fair share of shootouts this season.  The Week 1 matchup is unkind, though; the Cowboys will face the defending champion Philadelphia Eagles on Thursday. The Eagles allowed just 17.8 points per tilt in 2024, which was second in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.2: Brandon Aubrey connected on two field goals and two extra points in the season opener for Dallas. Aubrey is an outstanding 25-of-28 on field goals of 50-plus yards for his career. Aubrey should remain busy in Week 2 versus the Giants. New York allowed 21 points in their season opener, and Aubrey connected on at least two field goals and two extra points in each of the two matchups with the G-Men last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brandon Aubrey kicked the Dallas Cowboys to victory in Week 2. Aubrey's 64-yard field goal sent the game into overtime, while a mere 46-yarder clinched the victory over the Giants in a 40-37 thriller. Aubrey has made seven field goals thus far in 2025, five of which have come from 50-plus yards. Arguably the best kicker in football should be licking his chops ahead of a Week 3 clash with the bumbling Chicago Bears. Chicago is allowing the most points in the NFL through two contests.

player.seasonOutlook: A historically strong defense, the Ravens had 50-plus sacks in 2023 and 2024, the only NFL team to do that, and they roster two All-Pros (CB Marlon Humphrey and LB Roquan Smith) and second-team S Kyle Hamilton. The addition of first-round S Malaki Starks boosts their secondary, and the Ravens have a generally sound schedule including two games each against the Browns and Steelers. Watch out for that tough opening-week matchup (@BUF), however.

outlooksByWeek.1: Najee Harris jumped ship from the Steelers to the Chargers as a free agent this offseason, a move that landed him in an even more run-friendly offense scheme but also put him in competition with 2025 first-round pick Omarion Hampton for touches. Unfortunately for Harris, any shot he might have had of beginning the season with the top job ended when he suffered damage to his eyes in a Fourth of July fireworks accident. The veteran back missed all of training camp and the preseason, and while he should be cleared to play in Week 1 in Sao Paulo, his role figures to be limited as he gets up to game speed. Harris will likely struggle to make much of the snaps he collects against a Kansas City defense that ranked in the top four in both rushing yards and receiving yards allowed to RBs last season.
outlooksByWeek.2: Najee Harris was used sparingly in his Chargers debut, getting only two touches and turning them into 10 scrimmage yards. The veteran back's volume was affected by the time he missed in training camp due to a July fireworks accident, but he appeared to be 100% healthy when he rotated in. Rookie Omarion Hampton dominated the workload out of the backfield, and while Harris' role should grow as he ramps up, he may be stuck as the team's No. 2 RB rather than pushing for more of a 1A/1B split. He'll try to earn more touches in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that looked stout up front against the Patriots in its opener, and which ranked 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs in 2024.
outlooksByWeek.3: Najee Harris continues to put his July fireworks accident in the rearview mirror. After garnering only two touches in his Chargers' debut in Week 1, his workload increased to 10 touches in a Week 2 win over the Raiders, although he turned them into just 48 scrimmage yards. Rookie running back Omarion Hampton committed a fumble late in the win over Las Vegas, which gave Harris additional work on the final drives, and his perceived reliability might tip the workload scales further in his favor. The former Steeler will look to break out in Week 3 against a Broncos defense that just surrendered 215 scrimmage yards and a TD to the Colts' Jonathan Taylor.

player.seasonOutlook: Harris signed with the Chargers after spending his first four seasons in Pittsburgh. He is as durable as they come, as he's the only tailback who has appeared in 100% of his team's games over the past four seasons. He has yet to finish a season lower than seventh in the league in carries (255-plus each season), but that figures to change this season with first-round rookie Omarion Hampton likely to handle lead-back duties in Los Angeles. Harris also figures to be very limited as a receiver, as Jim Harbaugh and Greg Roman have a long history of low RB usage in the pass game, in addition to the fact Harris has finished outside the top 20 RBs in targets each of the past two seasons. Harris has ranked in the 20-to-30 range in fantasy PPG each of the past three seasons, but even if he splits carries with Hampton, he'll be hard-pressed to produce consistent flex numbers.

outlooksByWeek.1: Darnell Mooney looks to be the second option in Atlanta's passing game against Tampa Bay in Week 1. The former Bears receiver has been dealing with a shoulder problem this offseason, but he should be ready to go for the season opener. Mooney saw a huge improvement in 2024 after joining the Falcons, logging over 1,000 receiving yards even with a rough quarterback room. Quarterback Michael Penix will now lead the squad, which could be even better for Mooney if the second-year quarterback is any better than Kirk Cousins was. Mooney will have to play against a Buccaneers secondary in Week 1 that wasn't too tough for wide receivers in 2024.
outlooksByWeek.2: Darnell Mooney could make his season debut for the Falcons against the Vikings in Week 2. Mooney had to sit out of Atlanta's Week 1 opener as he's still dealing with a shoulder injury, but he could return to the field as soon as this upcoming week if he has a healthy slate of practices. The sixth-year wide receiver is now joined on the injury report by position mate Drake London, who suffered a shoulder sprain in Week 1. Mooney's return could be at a perfect time, given that Minnesota gave up 210 passing yards to quarterback Caleb Williams and 147 total receiving yards to Chicago's top-three pass catchers this past week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Darnell Mooney will aim to get more looks in Atlanta's offense during a Week 3 matchup at Carolina. Mooney totaled just four targets and brought in two for 20 yards in his season debut against the Vikings in Week 2. The Falcons did emphasize the run game in the defensive-dominated outing, and they finished the game with 38 carries among the two running backs. This ground-and-pound technique likely won't be utilized every week, and Mooney should garner a solid chunk of targets from quarterback Michael Penix when the passing game is at the forefront. With that being said, the Panthers have allowed the fourth-least fantasy points to wide receivers so far this season, so Mooney is a fringe flex play for the away game.

player.seasonOutlook: Mooney is entering his sixth NFL season, including his second with the Falcons. Year 1 in Atlanta was a relative success despite Mooney playing behind Drake London in a run-heavy offense. The veteran receiver handled a 21% target share and had his best showings in targets, catches and yards since his breakout 2021 season. He also caught a career-high five touchdowns. Though Mooney played well, the production wasn't enough to allow his first top-30 fantasy campaign (PPG). Mooney remains locked into the No. 2 WR role in a Falcons' offense that very well could make a leap with Michael Penix Jr. entering his first season as the full-time starting quarterback. That's enough to put him on the flex radar, but his upside is limited.

outlooksByWeek.1: Rachaad White and the Buccaneers have a Week 1 home matchup against a Falcons defense that excelled against running backs last season. White eventually lost the top running back role to Bucky Irving in the 2024 campaign, and this hierarchy is set to stay in place for 2025. While that is slightly discouraging for the incoming third-year rusher, White does still appeal as a passing-down back that excels in open space. This makes him more of a change-of-pace backfield option behind Irving against Atlanta, but White has shown that he can still provide some value for Tampa Bay given the right situation.
outlooksByWeek.2: Rachaad White is set to be the supplementary option for the Buccaneers in a Week 2 away game versus Houston. White had next-to-no output against the Falcons in Week 1, logging two carries for 14 yards and one catch for two yards. These totals were worse than all but two of his appearances last season, which means he could be slowly getting fazed out of a meaningful role with Tampa Bay. He'll aim to carve out any type of involvement and possibly tap into his receiving upside against a Texans team that gave 68 rushing yards, 17 receiving yards, and one rushing touchdown to Rams running backs in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rachaad White could continue to eat into Bucky Irving's touches as the Buccaneers play the Jets in Week 3. White scored the game-winning touchdown for Tampa Bay in Week 2 versus the Texans and finished the game with 12 total touches, but he still was outpaced by Irving. White's role doesn't look to be diminishing any time soon, but he is still definitely behind Irving on the totem pole. This backfield share could benefit both of them, though, against a Jets defense that has given up the fourth-most fantasy points to running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: White enters his fourth NFL season no longer positioned as Tampa Bay's lead back. The 2022 third-round pick peaked when he finished top 5 among RBs in snaps, touches, carries, routes, catches, yards and fantasy points during a breakout 2023 season, but his pedestrian efficiency led to a reduced role in 2024. White still scored nine TDs and ended up in the top 10 among RBs in targets, catches and receiving yards, but he fell to 23rd in fantasy PPG. One of only two backs with 50-plus receptions in each of the past three seasons (Alvin Kamara is the other), White figures to sustain a pass-catching role in a good offense, but Bucky Irving appears to be the new lead back in Tampa. White is a fine late-round insurance flier.

outlooksByWeek.1: Dylan Sampson was a fourth-round pick by the Browns in the 2025 draft and should immediately have a significant role heading into a Week 1 matchup against Cincinnati. For the time being, he will be joined by Jerome Ford in the backfield, and we're likely to see the duo split work relatively evenly in the short term. Sampson is a fine stash due to the uncertainty of Quinshon Judkins' status and Sampson's potential to take over the backfield, but he's best left on fantasy benches in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.2: Dylan Sampson wasted no time establishing himself as the lead back in Cleveland, as he out-touched Jerome Ford 20-7 in Week 1. The majority of Sampson's work came as a receiver, and he was highly inefficient as a rusher by averaging only 2.4 yards per carry. He'll face two primary challenges in Week 2, the first of which is a matchup with a Ravens defense that is projected to be among the better in the league despite getting exploited by the Bills in Week 1. Furthermore, Quinshon Judkins has the chance to be active, which would almost certainly cut into Sampson's volume. There are worse FLEX options, but he's ideally a player to stash on the bench until there's a better idea of how the Browns will allocate touches in the backfield.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dylan Sampson was heavily affected by the introduction of Quinshon Judkins into the Cleveland offense, as his total touches fell from 20 in Week 1 to seven in Week 2. He salvaged his day with an eight-yard touchdown reception late in a blowout loss to the Ravens, but that shouldn't fool fantasy managers into viewing him as a reliable fantasy option heading into a tough Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Sampson is fine as a bench stash, but he should not be slotted into fantasy lineups.

player.seasonOutlook: Sampson was selected by Cleveland in the fourth round of April's draft. He is one of the smallest and youngest RBs (20) in this class. He was an effective collegiate rusher (5.9 YPC), but wasn't used much in the pass game (1.5 targets per game). He's tough and makes plays, but his size could limit his touch ceiling. Sampson's fantasy outlook is less than ideal, as second-round rookie Quinshon Judkins is the team's short- and long-term lead back, with Jerome Ford possibly a factor in 2025 as well. Sampson is barely worth late-round consideration, but is a fine dynasty hold.

outlooksByWeek.1: Christian Kirk could begin the season as the second option in Houston's passing game behind Nico Collins, though Kirk will have competition from rookie Day 2 draft picks Jayden Higgins and Jaylin Noel in Week 1 against the Rams. The Texans traded for Kirk in the offseason, and the former Jaguars wide receiver has recovered from the collarbone injury that cut his 2024 campaign short, but Kirk's Week 1 status is now in jeopardy due to a hamstring injury. If healthy enough to play, Kirk figures to work primarily in the slot as he looks to reverse the downward trend from his time in Jacksonville, where the 28-year-old WR had a career-high 1,108 receiving yards in 17 games in 2022, then 787 yards in 12 games in 2023, and only 379 yards in eight games last season. Kirk has the edge in experience over Higgins and Noel but also the most questions about his health.
outlooksByWeek.2: Christian Kirk sat out Houston's opener due to a hamstring injury. His Texans debut could come in Week 2 against the Buccaneers, but while Kirk has an extra day to heal since Houston plays on Monday Night Football, he also carries more risk due to the limited alternatives available for fantasy managers who plan to start Kirk if he plays. Once healthy, Kirk figures to occupy the slot role for the Texans, competing with rookie second-round pick Jayden Higgins for targets behind No. 1 WR Nico Collins. Tampa Bay allowed the seventh-most receiving yards to WRs in 2024, so Kirk has some deep-league flex appeal if he gets good news on the injury front.
outlooksByWeek.3: Christian Kirk is working his way back from a hamstring injury that prevented him from playing in the first two games of the season. However, head coach DeMeco Ryans said Tuesday that he anticipates the veteran wideout will suit up to face his former team, the Jaguars, in Week 3. The potential return of Kirk could provide a much-needed boost in the slot, as the Texans' passing attack ranks 28th in the NFL with an average of 166.5 yards per game through the first two weeks. He'll have to compete for targets with Jayden Higgins and Xavier Hutchinson, as well as tight end Dalton Schultz. Still, Kirk's elusiveness and pass-catching ability make him a potential flex option in deep formats. However, even that would depend on quarterback C.J. Stroud taking a leap compared to his previous two outings.

player.seasonOutlook: Kirk was traded to Houston after spending his first seven NFL seasons in Arizona and Jacksonville. He peaked in 2022 when he posted career-high marks across the board and finished 18th among WRs in fantasy PPG, but that marks his only career top-30 season. Last season, he missed nine games and, while he did have a few solid outings (12-plus points three weeks in a row), he averaged a career-low 8.9 PPG on the season. With Tank Dell (knee) in doubt for 2025, Kirk will compete with rookies Jayden Higgins and Jaylin Noel for No. 2 receiver duties opposite Nico Collins, and he figures to work as the team's primary slot receiver. There's not much upside here (he's cleared six TDs once in his career), so Kirk should be viewed as no more than a late-round pick.

outlooksByWeek.1: Wan'Dale Robinson garnered almost nine targets per game for the Giants last season, dominating the shorter routes as a possession receiver to complement Malik Nabers. Robinson finished the season with 93 catches for 699 yards and three touchdowns.  Russell Wilson is the new quarterback under center, but Robinson should continue to figure prominently in the passing attack, as the Giants did not bring in any other wideouts as compared to last season to compete for looks. In Week 1, though, Robinson will face a tough task against Washington on Sunday. The Commanders boasted a stellar pass defense in 2024, allowing only 189.5 passing yards per outing, which was third in the league.
outlooksByWeek.2: Wan'Dale Robinson picked up where he left off last season in Week 1 for the Giants.  The possession receiver snagged six passes for 55 yards on eight targets, though the Giants fell by a score of 21-6 to the Commanders. New starting quarterback Russell Wilson struggled, passing for just 168 yards for the game and failing to lead a single touchdown drive. Robinson could be catching passes from rookie Jaxson Dart sooner than anticipated, though the switch is not likely to occur in Week 2 versus the Cowboys. Dallas held up surprisingly well in Week 1 versus the Eagles, allowing only 144 yards passing and zero touchdowns through the air.
outlooksByWeek.3: Wan'Dale Robinson posted a career-high 142 receiving yards for the Giants last game. Normally a possession receiver, Robinson got free for several large chunk plays en route to the best numbers of his brief career. Robinson has 14 catches on 18 targets through just two games. In Week 3, the Giants will face a hungry Kansas City squad that is also 0-2 to start the season, with a defense was picked apart by Justin Herbert in Week 1, but bounced back in Week 2 by allowing just 101 passing yards and zero throwing scores to the Eagles.

player.seasonOutlook: Robinson is entering his fourth NFL season following a breakout 2024 campaign. The 2022 second-round pick was limited to 838 yards and three TDs on 94 touches during his first two seasons (21 games), but made the leap to 717 yards and three TDs on 96 touches in 17 games while playing alongside Malik Nabers in 2024. Despite handling a hefty 25% target share (which helped him to top-10 finishes in both targets and receptions), Robinson finished outside the top 40 receivers in yardage and fantasy PPG due to a WR-low 4.9 aDOT and horrific 5.0 YPT. The 24-year-old is strictly a short-area option and, though having Russell Wilson (and perhaps Jaxson Dart) under center will help, Robinson is a very low-ceiling PPR depth receiver.

teams.name: Sorry Mr Jackson, I am for Hill
